```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

memdash is a Shiny dashboard for [Memgraph](https://memgraph.com). It connects
over **Bolt** using the official Python `neo4j` driver through **reticulate**,
so plain openCypher works unmodified.

## 1. Prerequisites

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# Python driver in the reticulate Python environment
reticulate::py_install("neo4j")

# Install this package
devtools::install("r-package/memdash")
```

Start Memgraph, e.g.:

```bash
docker run -p 7687:7687 memgraph/memgraph
```

## 2. Launch the dashboard

```{r, eval = FALSE}
memdash::run_memdash()
```

In the app: set **Bolt URI** to `bolt://localhost:7687`, press **Connect**,
then **Load demo data** and **Run all**.

## 3. Use it in code

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(memdash)

memgraph_connect("bolt://localhost:7687")
memdash_seed_demo()

# Metric
res <- memgraph_query("MATCH (n) RETURN count(n) AS nodes")
records_to_df(res$records, res$fields)

# Graph card data
res <- memgraph_query("MATCH (n)-[r]->(m) RETURN n, r, m LIMIT 50")
g <- records_to_graph(res$records)
length(g$nodes)  # visNetwork-ready nodes
length(g$edges)  # visNetwork-ready edges

# Parameters ($limit is substituted as a quoted literal)
memgraph_query("MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name AS name LIMIT $limit",
               params = list(limit = "10"))

memgraph_disconnect()
```

## 4. Custom cards

```{r, eval = FALSE}
cards <- default_cards()
cards[[1]]$cypher <- "MATCH (n:Person) RETURN count(n) AS people"
memdash_app(cards = cards)
```
